s.t: Richard Hell’s ‘Blank Generation’ is a rewrite of Bob McFadden and Rod McKuen’s 1959 record ‘The Beat Generation’; he wrote the new lyrics while in Television.
s.q: A rewrite of Bob McFadden and Rod McKuen's 1959 record "The Beat Generation", Richard Hell wrote the new lyrics during his time with the band Television

s.t: Malcolm McLaren claimed that the Sex Pistols’ ‘Pretty Vacant’ was directly inspired by Richard Hell’s ‘Blank Generation’.
s.q: Malcolm McLaren claimed that the Sex Pistols' song "Pretty Vacant" was directly inspired by "Blank Generation".

s.t: Rapper Amil heavily sampled Richard Hell’s ‘Blank Generation’ in 2000, on her track ‘Get Down’ from the album All Money Is Legal.
s.q: In 2000, "Blank Generation" was heavily sampled on rapper Amil's track "Get Down" on her album All Money Is Legal.

s.t: A March 1974 CBGB recording of Richard Hell’s ‘Blank Generation’ with Television is on Spurts: The Richard Hell Story; the Heartbreakers’ July 1975 CBGB version is on What Goes Around...
s.q: An earlier live recording by the Heartbreakers, recorded at CBGB on July 7, 1975, appeared on the What Goes Around... album. A live March 1974 recording at CBGB with Television can be found on Spurts: The Richard Hell Story.

f.t: He and Tom Verlaine published poems as Theresa Stern, a fictional poet whose photo combined both their faces in drag; Dot released her book Wanna Go Out? in 1973.
f.q: In 1971, along with Verlaine, Hell also published under the pseudonym Theresa Stern, a fictional poet whose photo was actually a combination of both his and Verlaine's faces in drag

f.t: He left Television in early 1975 after a dispute over creative control, then formed the Heartbreakers with Jerry Nolan and Johnny Thunders, who had just quit the New York Dolls.
f.q: In early 1975, Hell parted ways with Television after a dispute over creative control. Hell left Television the same week that Jerry Nolan and Johnny Thunders quit the New York Dolls. In May 1975, the three of them formed the Heartbreakers

f.t: In 1986 he and Legs McNeil spent several days on the Mississippi River in inflatable rubber rafts, from Hannibal, Missouri to Hamburg, Illinois, marking a century of Huckleberry Finn.
f.q: In 1986, to commemorate the publication of Adventures of Huckleberry Finn by Mark Twain one hundred years before, Hell and Legs McNeil spent several days on the Mississippi River in inflatable rubber rafts, starting in Hannibal, Missouri and ending in Hamburg, Illinois.

f.t: New York University’s Fales Library bought his archive of manuscripts, tapes, correspondence and journals in 2003 for $50,000.
f.q: Hell's archive of his manuscripts, tapes, correspondence (written and email), journals and other documents of his life was purchased for $50,000 by New York University's Fales Library in 2003.

f.t: He had a non-speaking cameo as Madonna’s murdered boyfriend in Susan Seidelman’s 1985 film Desperately Seeking Susan.
f.q: Hell had a non-speaking cameo role as Madonna's murdered boyfriend in Seidelman's 1985 Desperately Seeking Susan.
